description: We have combined our experience in full-stack software development, DevOps, embedded systems, and applied mathematics to work on astronaut health monitoring and real-time telemetry analytics. We are FULL and the roles in a team are already settled down. It will be very hard to integrate new participants.
summary: VITALIS+ is a full-stack deep-space health monitoring and decision-support platform built for NASA’s five Human Research Program (HRP) spaceflight hazards: Space Radiation, Isolation & Confinement, Distance from Earth, Altered Gravity Fields, and Hostile/Closed Environments.  Beyond low Earth orbit, communication delays reach up to 44 minutes round-trip and crews operate without an onboard flight surgeon. Instead of burying fatigued astronauts under raw vital-sign charts, VITALIS+ combines live NASA DONKI space-weather alerts, NASA JPL Horizons Earth–Mars ephemeris, NASA OSDR ISS cabin CO2 datasets, Supabase telemetry persistence, and a multi-mode Python simulator into deterministic hazard evaluators. Every screen translates complex biometrics and habitat readings into an immediate operational status (NOMINAL, ELEVATED, CRITICAL), an Estimated Time of Action (ETA), and 1–2 prioritized countermeasures. Role-Based Access Control gives mission commanders visibility into crew-wide readiness and shared habitat stressors while keeping private behavioral self-checks strictly scoped to each astronaut.By turning fragmented telemetry into clear, privacy-preserving, time-critical guidance,VITALIS+ empowers crews to detect shared threats early and act autonomously far from Earth.
details:
What VITALIS+ Does & How It Works

VITALIS+ is an autonomous deep-space crew health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for long-duration missions beyond low Earth orbit, where Earth communication delays can reach 44 minutes round-trip and no dedicated physician is on board.

The platform is built around all five NASA Human Research Program (HRP) spaceflight hazards, backed by Supabase Postgres persistence (scenarios, crew slots, latest stream snapshots, and time-series samples) and deterministic TypeScript evaluation pipelines:

1. Space Radiation: Pulls live space-weather events (SEP, FLR, RBE, CME) from NASA DONKI, performs trapezoidal cumulative dose integration on personal dosimeters while strictly preventing silent mixing of incompatible dose families (mSv vs. mGy), detects compartment sensor disagreements, and provides emergency shelter and what-if simulation views.

2. Isolation & Confinement: Evaluates actigraphy sleep duration and circadian phase drift alongside habitat acoustics, lighting schedules, mission progress, private 60-second behavioral self-checks, and CONNECT countermeasure logs.

3. Distance from Earth: Integrates directly with the NASA JPL Horizons API to query Earth–Mars ephemeris distances by UTC date, compute one-way and round-trip signal latency with solar conjunction hysteresis, track autonomous onboard medical kit inventory, and persist updates to Supabase.

4. Altered Gravity Fields: Monitors daily resistive/aerobic exercise adherence and tracks musculoskeletal and fluid-shift deconditioning across separate measurement cadences (14-day calf circumference and 30-day handgrip strength) with pre-test condition screening.

5. Hostile & Closed Environments: Renders an interactive 4-module Habitat Air Map (Lab, Habitat, Galley, Airlock) evaluating CO2, O2, total cabin pressure, and acoustics against NASA OCHMO operational bounds, replays real ISS cabin CO2 telemetry from NASA OSDR (RR-1_EDA_Telemetry_table.csv), fits a 30-minute linear regression to project +2 hour CO2 trends against a 3.80 mmHg early-warning line and NASA's 4.00 mmHg limit, calculates headache odds multipliers, tracks cumulative exposure minutes, and supports persistent alert acknowledgement. A companion Python CLI telemetry simulator seeds and streams telemetry in real time across four modes (demo, positive, negative, and chaos stress testing) either directly to Supabase or through the Next.js API.

Benefits & Intended Impact

• Action-First Clarity: Instead of burying fatigued astronauts under raw multi-chart vital logs, every hazard screen surfaces one clear operational state (NOMINAL, ELEVATED, CRITICAL), an Estimated Time of Action (ETA), and 1–2 prioritized countermeasures.

• Team-Wide vs. Individual Diagnosis: Correlating shared cabin and space-weather telemetry helps commanders spot collective environmental threats (e.g., rising module CO2 or solar particle storms) early rather than treating symptoms as isolated illness.

• Medical Privacy in Command Views: Role-Based Access Control lets Mission Leads monitor full-crew operational readiness while stripping private psychological self-check fields (private mood valence, personal journal notes, sleep medication flags) before data reaches client views. Crew Members see only their own telemetry plus shared mission streams.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

• Frontend & API: Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript 5.8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons, Space HUD typography (Roboto, Audiowide, Anonymous Pro).

• Database: Supabase Postgres (@supabase/supabase-js) with Next.js Route Handlers.

• Telemetry Simulator: Python 3 with supabase, python-dotenv, and requests.

• NASA Data & Standards: NASA DONKI API, NASA JPL Horizons API, NASA OSDR Environmental Data App (ISS RR-1 dataset), NASA-STD-3001, and NASA OCHMO Technical Briefs.

• Testing & Deployment: Node.js built-in test runner (radiation & RBAC unit tests), ESLint, TypeScript compiler checks, GitHub, and Vercel (Landing: https://vitalis-three-teal.vercel.app/ · Live App:

https://vitalis-nasa-hackathon-2026-nine.vercel.app/).

How It Is Creative

• Translates complex NASA OCHMO / HRP thresholds into a cohesive dark Space HUD featuring an interactive 4-module habitat air map, dual-horizon CO2 forecast charts, and inline (i) Research Citation Modals linking every metric directly to its primary NASA reference.

• Includes a dedicated Chaos telemetry mode alongside Positive and Negative modes so teams can stress-test ingestion pipelines, unit-safety guards, alert triage, and ETA countdowns under simultaneous multi-system failures.

Key Engineering Factors Considered

• Dimensional & Unit Safety: Radiation evaluators explicitly reject invalid cross-family math (e.g., integrating absorbed dose in Gy with equivalent dose in Sv).

• Data Provenance Transparency: Environment readouts explicitly separate REAL NASA OSDR telemetry tags from SIMULATED values, and JPL Horizons queries clearly note ephemeris calculation vs. live spacecraft telemetry.

• Security & Privacy Boundaries: Server-side RBAC enforces Lead vs. Member visibility, while Next.js middleware protects against local DNS rebinding and cross-origin CSRF API mutations.
